summary: As of October 1, 2026, junk-bond spreads widened by 0.44 percentage points over the previous five trading days, led by the riskiest bonds, called CCC, which widened by 1.03 percentage points. High-yield spreads are 3.24 percentage points, the 75th percentile of the 786 days still on file since October 3, 2023, investment-grade spreads are 0.86 percentage points, the 53rd percentile of the 785 days still on file since October 3, 2023, and BB spreads are 2.04 percentage points, the 81st percentile of the 786 days still on file since October 3, 2023. The five-day pace is a move of 0.44 percentage points, versus 0.10 percentage points over the five days before that, so the pace is speeding up by 0.34 percentage points, and the gap between CCC and BB bonds is 10.11 percentage points, and the all-in junk yield moved 0.42 percentage points over five days, of which 0.44 was the credit spread and 0.02 was Treasury rates, so this is stress climbing through the junk market, not a market-wide credit problem.
what_would_change_this: This would become a market-wide credit problem if BB bonds reached 2.22 percentage points, or the top 10 percent of the days still on file, and investment-grade bonds widened by at least 0.10 percentage points over five trading days or 0.15 percentage points over twenty trading days.
description: Credit monitor rebuilt from FRED. Each value keeps the observation date FRED published. Nothing is copied forward onto a newer date.

methodology.stale_rule: stale is true when the latest real observation is more than 2 US equity business days older than the New York run date. Age of 2 is not stale.
methodology.business_day_calendar: Weekdays minus the regular NYSE holiday schedule. One-off closures are not listed.
methodology.percentile: Empirical percentile: 100 times the share of observations in the window that are less than or equal to the latest value. The window label, start date, end date, and n_days are the whole description. Do not call it 5-year.
methodology.changes: 1-day, 5-day, and 20-day changes step back that many real observations. The 3-month change uses the last real print on or before the calendar day three months earlier.
methodology.yield_split: Treasury part of the high-yield yield change equals the yield change in basis points minus the OAS change in basis points.
regime_rules: SYSTEMIC if BB's level is elevated AND investment-grade OAS is widening.
BROADENING if BB is widening AND CCC is leading, and the SYSTEMIC rule did not fire.
CONCENTRATED if CCC is leading AND BB is not widening, and the SYSTEMIC rule did not fire.
CALM if none of those rules fire.
UNKNOWN if every 5-day input is missing.
Rules are checked in that order. The first match wins.
Widening means the spread rose by at least the threshold. A decline does not count as moving wider.
CCC is leading if CCC's own spread is widening, or the CCC-minus-BB gap is widening.
BB is elevated if its percentile over the full available FRED sample is at least 90, or its level is at least 222 bp (the March 2026 reference).
The percentile is never labeled 5-year. FRED's ICE BofA history is only as long as the file says (window_start and n_days).

units.bp: Basis points. 100 bp = 1 percentage point. Spread levels and all spread and yield changes use bp.
units.percent: Percent, already in percentage points. 8.16 means 8.16 percent, not 816 bp.
units.percentile: A number from 0 to 100. 100 means the latest value is the high of the window.

methodology.publish_rule: A run commits this file only when official_as_of contains a date newer than the copy already stored, or when the plain-English summary is missing. The same observation date never produces a second commit, and rows are never duplicated.

frontend_notes: Every measurement has a numeric value and a separate unit field. Display the number once and the unit once. Do not append 'bp' or 'bps' if you already included the unit.
Draw distribution markers from the numeric value. Passing a string such as '968 bps' makes the marker math fail and the dot sits on the minimum.
null means FRED had no print that day. Do not copy the previous day's number into that cell.

regime.label: BROADENING
regime.plain_english: BROADENING. CCC and BB are both widening, so stress is climbing from the weakest junk into better junk. BB's level is not extreme, and investment-grade spreads are calm. The high-yield minus investment-grade gap is widening.

credit_speed.definition: Today's 5-observation change in the high-yield spread, using only real FRED dates. Acceleration is that number minus the same 5-observation change from 5 observations earlier. Increasing means the pace itself picked up.

acceleration.rule: increasing when acceleration is +5 bp or more, decreasing when it is -5 bp or less, otherwise steady.

change_in_speed_1d.note: Today's 5-day change minus yesterday's 5-day change. This is a one-step tick. The direction word uses acceleration versus 5 observations ago, not this tick.

credit_speed.plain_english: The 5-day pace is faster than it was 5 trading observations ago.

yield_decomposition.note: Each window splits the change in the high-yield all-in yield into the spread part and the Treasury-rate part. Treasury part = yield change minus spread change. Dates are the spread series' own dates. If the yield has no print on one of those dates, that window is left blank.

5d.label: 5 trading observations
5d.note: Treasury part = all-in yield change minus spread change, both in basis points. It will not exactly equal the 5-year, 10-year, or 30-year move. Those are shown beside it.

20d.label: 20 trading observations
20d.note: Treasury part = all-in yield change minus spread change, both in basis points. It will not exactly equal the 5-year, 10-year, or 30-year move. Those are shown beside it.

3m.label: 3 calendar months
3m.note: Treasury part = all-in yield change minus spread change, both in basis points. It will not exactly equal the 5-year, 10-year, or 30-year move. Those are shown beside it.
